title: Module quiz: End-to-end and multi-agent architecture

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario: Fenwick Bank's design review turns up two problems, one rated medium and one rated high. What outcome does the rubric give?

options.text: Revise, because the medium problem is the one that can be repaired most easily
options.says: Ruled out because "any `high` gives `reject`, otherwise any `medium` gives `revise`".

options.text: Reject, since the worst item governs the result
options.says: The verdict follows the worst finding, and a `high` gives `reject`.

options.text: Approve, because a medium and a high problem cancel each other out
options.says: Ruled out because "The verdict follows the worst finding" and nothing cancels it.

options.text: Revise, because the two ratings are averaged into one level of severity
options.says: Ruled out because there is no averaging: "otherwise any `medium` gives `revise`, otherwise `approve`".

origin.section: An architecture review as a rubric

questions.stem: Scenario: Willow Bank's complaint triage design collects a rating from customers for every reply and stores the ratings in a table that nobody reads. How should the review treat the feedback stage?

options.text: As present, since a rating is collected for every reply that customers receive
options.says: Ruled out because collecting a rating is logging and not a loop: the stage holds "Evaluation, logging, human corrections, and the path by which they change the system".

options.text: As absent, since no path leads from those scores to a change in the system
options.says: The stage is defined by "the path by which they change the system", and here there is none.

options.text: As present, once the ratings table is backed up on a regular schedule
options.says: Ruled out because backups protect the table and do not change the system, and the cost of the gap is that "Nobody learns that it was wrong".

options.text: As absent only if the table holds fewer than a thousand rows of ratings
options.says: Ruled out because the size of a table does not decide the finding, and a pipeline that "never learns from the result" goes wrong whatever its volume.

origin.section: Four stages that every end-to-end design has

questions.stem: Scenario: Quince Retail runs a returns agent that writes refunds to the ledger without approval, and the auditors require a record of each approval. What does the rubric report?

options.text: A medium finding, because the missing approval can be added during later testing
options.says: Ruled out because "The verdict follows the worst finding", and the rubric names `high` for this one.

options.text: No finding, since the agent's answers have already been validated before the write
options.says: Ruled out because the rule fires when "The design writes without approval and an audit is needed", whatever was validated.

options.text: A finding about autonomy, since the path of a return is known in advance
options.says: Ruled out because that finding applies only when "An agent or a team is used on a path that is already known".

options.text: A high finding, which makes the verdict reject whatever the cost of the design
options.says: A write without approval where an audit is needed is a `high` finding, so the verdict is reject.
